name: bubble-level
title: Bubble level
summary: A spirit level: a green bubble offset from the centre by the accelerometer's X and Y readings, clamped to a circle inside the dial.
prompt: Build a bubble level that uses the phone's accelerometer to move a bubble around a round dial.
teaches: Read the device tilt with accelerationX() and accelerationY() (m/s², about ±9.8 at 90°) inside an expression
Clamp a 2-D offset to a circle: scale it by 72 / max(hypot(dx, dy), 72), which is 1 inside the radius
Compute the bubble position once in canvas variables and reuse it for the bubble and its highlight

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()

snippets.note: dx = -8 * accelerationX(): the bubble rises against the tilt

check.describe: With no sensor input the bubble sits in the centre ring; system_variables {17: 4, 18: -3} move it up and to the left; {17: 9, 18: -9} pins it to the dial's edge on the diagonal, still inside the dial. Resized, the background fills the box and the level (dial, cross-hair and bubble travel) scales to the shorter side, centred.

pitfalls: Clamping x and y separately (min/max per axis) keeps the bubble in a square, so on a diagonal it leaves a round dial; clamp the length of the offset instead
accelerationX/Y are 0 with no sensor (and in a static render), so the default state is the bubble centred; pin system variables 17 and 18 to preview a tilt
The sign is a design choice: a real bubble moves toward the raised side, i.e. opposite to the acceleration on that axis

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one
